  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Experimental person-level bootstrap intervals}

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(repair)
```

`repair_bootstrap()` samples **whole people with replacement** and calls
`repair_refit()` to rebuild the complete analysis. Each selected occurrence gets
fresh person and nuisance IDs. Measurement models, scores, score-error covariance,
structural moments, corrections, and weights are re-estimated for each attempt.
The original fit and its conditional inference remain available for comparison.

This functionality is **experimental**: software replay tests verify the
calculation, while targeted simulation screens show condition-dependent coverage.
Broader independent coverage validation remains outstanding.
It assumes independent people. It does not remedy dependence across people,
misspecification, informative missingness, or weak identification.

## Fit, sample, and report

When repeated measurement refits produce convergence warnings, select a fitting
strategy before running the bootstrap. `repair_lmer_refitter()` uses a
deterministic nloptwrap starting fit followed by likelihood-checked BOBYQA and,
when needed, bounded retries. Use it to fit the **original** measurement model:

```{r robust-recipe, eval=FALSE}
fitter <- repair_lmer_refitter(score ~ day + (day | person))
model <- fitter(repair_example$repeated)
fit <- repair(re("day") ~ practice, model, repair_example$people, "person")
boot <- repair_bootstrap(fit, repair_example$repeated,
                         repair_example$people, B = 1999, seed = 214)
repair_bootstrap_diagnostics(boot)$optimization[[1]]
attr(model, "repair_lmer_optimization")
```

The model retains its recipe, so reference and resampled fits use it automatically,
including after saving/loading. Do not add a different optimizer strategy only
to failed bootstrap draws from an existing analysis: rebuild the original fit
with the chosen recipe first. Every optimizer attempt is retained in the audit;
an unresolved convergence or likelihood check still withholds default inference.
Retries do not add bootstrap draws, change the measurement model or structural
regularization, or consume random numbers. Singular fits alone are not failures.
This improves numerical fitting; it does not establish coverage, remove estimator
bias, or justify dropping failed attempts. The robust helper currently covers
Gaussian lmer models; nlme replay remains unchanged.

```{r fit}
data(repair_example)
repeated <- repair_example$repeated
people <- repair_example$people
model <- lme4::lmer(score ~ day + (day | person), repeated,
  control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)))
fit <- repair(re("day") ~ practice, model, people, "person")

# Nine attempts make this guide quick to run; they are not adequate for inference.
boot <- repair_bootstrap(fit, repeated, people, B = 9, seed = 41)
summary(boot)
```

The default is `B = 1999`, counting **attempts**, with reproducible `seed = 1`.
Real analyses need sufficient tail resolution and checks of stability over larger
B and different seeds. Neither a large B nor a high success rate establishes
coverage. A run rebuilds the measurement model repeatedly, so it can take much
longer than the original structural analysis.

```{r inference}
coef(boot)                           # original-data estimates
vcov(boot)                           # empirical bootstrap covariance
confint(boot, level = .90)            # marginal percentile intervals
repair_bootstrap_coefficients(boot, conf.level = .90)
repair_coefficients(fit, conf.level = .90)  # original conditional Wald comparison
```

Bootstrap SEs are SDs of complete usable coefficient vectors. Percentile endpoints
are their empirical quantiles using R's `quantile(type = 7)`. The same vectors
are used for all coefficients and the joint covariance. Bootstrap variance is
**not added** to conditional variance. These are marginal intervals, not a
simultaneous confidence region. There are no bootstrap p-values or bootstrap
Wald z-statistics in the table.

## Examine attempts and reproduce a sampled analysis

```{r attempts}
attempts <- repair_bootstrap_diagnostics(boot)
attempts[, c("replicate", "usable", "stage", "n_people", "n_measurement",
  "measurement_singular", "preliminary_multiplier", "final_multiplier")]

mapping <- repair_bootstrap_diagnostics(boot, "draws")
head(mapping)
```

Each mapping row identifies `(replicate, draw, source_id, refit_id)`. Repeated
source IDs within a replicate correspond to distinct people in that refit.
Generated IDs are reused between independently fitted replicates, so always keep
the replicate key. Character source IDs, including leading zeros, stay intact.

For example, replay the first recorded sample without generating another one:

```{r reproduce}
first_ids <- mapping$source_id[mapping$replicate == 1L]
first <- repair_refit(fit, repeated, people, draw = first_ids)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(coef(first)), unname(boot$replicates[1, ]),
  tolerance = 1e-6)))
```

All effective observations for a sampled person are copied in their original
order, including unequal observation counts and schedules. There is no resampling
of observations within people. Contained nuisance groups such as `person:day`
remain separate for duplicate people. See the [refitting guide](refitting.html)
for exact replay, row/coding rules, supported lmer/lme settings, and explicit
`refitter(data)` callbacks. Each attempt uses that same reference validation.

## Failures are part of the result

A lost factor level, unusable score, measurement nonconvergence, or structural
failure invalidates the whole coefficient vector. The attempt stays in the result
with its source-ID map, stage, reason, warnings/messages when available, and an
all-NA coefficient row. There are no replacement bootstrap samples, trimming, or
within-attempt omission to rescue a fit. A recorded robust measurement recipe can
retry numerical optimization within the same sample and records every internal
fit in the `optimization` list-column. Singular lmer fits are retained when
convergence, scoring, and structural estimation remain usable; lme singularity is
not assessed. Warnings alone do not automatically invalidate an attempt.

This deliberately sparse factor demonstrates why successful samples can be a
selected distribution:

```{r failed-attempts}
sparse_people <- people
sparse_people$rare <- factor(seq_len(nrow(people)) == 1L)
sparse_fit <- repair(re("day") ~ practice + rare, model, sparse_people, "person")
sparse_boot <- repair_bootstrap(sparse_fit, repeated, sparse_people, B = 10, seed = 41)
summary(sparse_boot)  # remains inspectable; intervals are withheld
failed <- repair_bootstrap_diagnostics(sparse_boot)
failed[!failed$usable, c("replicate", "stage", "reason")]
```

If any attempt fails, `vcov()`, `confint()`, and the bootstrap coefficient
extractor stop by default. Investigate the reasons and the original model first.
Explicitly requesting `allow_failed = TRUE` gives a summary **conditional on
successful replicates**; it does not recover the distribution of all attempts:

```{r conditional-on-success}
repair_bootstrap_coefficients(sparse_boot, allow_failed = TRUE)
```

Counts and the changed interpretation appear in the table and summary. Covariance
and interval matrices carry counts, method, conditional-on-success status, and
an experimental label as attributes. At least two complete vectors are required
even after opt-in. This is only a numerical minimum, not a precision or validity
criterion. `B = 1` and runs with no usable vectors remain useful for diagnostics.

## Cohort and inference boundaries

The first implementation supports **one referenced measurement model**: Gaussian
lmer, including contained nuisance groups, or supported single-group linear lme.
The measurement and analyzed person cohorts must coincide. Measurement-only people
or people omitted structurally despite having measurement data require an
explicitly revised reference fit before sampling. The source order is the original
analysis order. Sampling conditions on the chosen cohort, selection rule, and
observed missingness pattern; it does not generate new within-person histories.

Structural and measurement IDs may use different column names. The target must
be a bare measurement ID; IDs used as substantive covariates and unsupported
nuisance mappings cannot be automatically re-keyed. Shared nuisance effects
remain rejected. Factor coding and coefficient identities remain fixed;
losing a level invalidates an attempt rather than changing the estimand.

Regularization policy/custom alpha, ML/REML, optimizer and covariance recipes,
formula, and computation backend follow the reference fit. Data-dependent
regularization multipliers and weights are recomputed; transitions in those
quantities can affect the distribution. Scores remain random deviations rather
than fixed-plus-random totals, and re-estimated fixed effects can change centering.

No stratification, higher-level cluster sampling, multiple-model bootstrap,
cross-model covariance replay, parallel execution, checkpoints/resume, BCa,
studentized, or simultaneous intervals are included. The next scientific gate is
a larger independent coverage study across reliability, sample size, design imbalance,
variance boundaries, and weak corrected moments.

## Reproducibility and saved results

The serial engine assigns one L'Ecuyer-CMRG stream to preflight and a separate
stream to each attempt, using Inversion normals and Rejection sampling. A fitting
failure or RNG use in one attempt cannot change subsequent samples. Extending B
with the same seed/data/recipe preserves the initial attempts in the same numerical
environment. `boot$rng` stores those streams; `boot$replicates` is the B-by-p
coefficient matrix. These are documented result fields, including all failed rows.

The caller's RNG kind and `.Random.seed` (including its absence) are restored on
success or error. Box-Muller and user-supplied caller RNGs are rejected before
changing state: their hidden state cannot be restored from `.Random.seed`.
Callbacks remain deterministic, explicit fitting recipes; no guarantee is made
for callbacks with external state or changing global options.

Save the bootstrap object with `saveRDS()` and reload with `readRDS()` after loading
`repair`. Extraction needs no original data bindings. The result stores original
estimates, the conditional comparison table, draws, attempts, reference audit,
streams, and versions. `boot$specification` records formula text, selected effects,
ID column, observable measurement settings, structural backend, and regularization
controls without formula environments or raw datasets. It retains neither every fitted replicate model nor copied
raw datasets. Retain original inputs, fitting code, and `sessionInfo()` separately
to rerun the analysis. Optimizer/dependency changes can affect numerical results;
cross-version bitwise equivalence is not promised.

The [R RNG-stream documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/parallel/html/RngStream.html)
describes the stream mechanism, and the
[R quantile documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/quantile.html)
specifies the percentile endpoint calculation. Neither establishes scientific
coverage for REPAIR; see the developer bootstrap design and implementation audit
in the repository for the outstanding validation plan.
